title: Insurance Programme
summary: Every insurance question used to be a request to a colleague: search the share drive, count by hand, reply hours or days later. I linked fifteen years of records once, then answered the fixed questions with dashboards and everything else with an assistant. Live, in daily use.

facts.label: Timeline
facts.value: Jun – Dec 2026 · live since September, handover by mid-October

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Data model, dashboards, assistant, auto report, mobile layout

facts.label: Stack
facts.value: Feishu Bitable / Spark / Aily · React · NestJS · LLM API for report drafts

sections.heading: The loop
paragraphs: A manager asks. The insurance team opens the share drive, finds the files, counts by hand, writes a short reply. Hours, sometimes days. Nothing is reused, so the next question starts the loop again.

sections.heading: Link once, answer two ways
paragraphs: The records were never wrong, just kept in three places that only referred to each other by number. Linking them once turned finding into clicking: open a class, its policies and claims come with it, each policy with its PDF attached.
Recurring questions became dashboards. Everything else goes to the assistant, which also drafts the report when a dashboard has to be shared.
bullets: Scope — it answers only from our tables and the policy documents inside them
Law — legal points cite the references we specified, for a specialist to confirm
Tools — it reads the policy PDFs and draws its own charts
sections.quote: Every number can be traced back to a source record. It is computed from the database, not counted and typed in.

sections.heading: Before → after
paragraphs: Look it up or ask → open the dashboard or ask the assistant. Nothing to search: the records are already linked. Export in one click: the report writes itself from the same records. The same system is re-laid out for the phone, not shrunk.

sections.heading: What the public demo withholds
paragraphs: The employer is not named. Aggregates are synthetic and badged as such; record-level fields render as explicit "Redacted" bars; the assistant is a visual replica that says so instead of inventing answers.
